entries.narrative: MF-030 closes a silent failure of the epic's binding complexity gate. analyze_complexity.py read one .tla file and stopped at EXTENDS, so on the decomposed architecture SKILL.md mandates it scored only the declarations literally present in the analyzed file. The error is never conservative: missing variables only ever shrink the product bound, so the gate failed toward PASS on exactly the shape the skill requires. MF-023 measured External reporting bound = 1 over 2 of 9 variables from this. The fix is a partial module resolver (resolve_module) that follows EXTENDS through the hierarchy and unions VARIABLES, CONSTANTS, and the top-level definitions carrying TypeInvariant/Init/actions, base-first with the extending module overriding inherited names. Standard TLA+ library modules (Naturals, Integers, Reals, Sequences, FiniteSets, Bags, TLC, Json) declare no VARIABLES the bound reads and are skipped rather than resolved to a file. Every construct the resolver cannot model FAILS CLOSED with a named error rather than under-reporting: INSTANCE / named and unnamed instantiation, WITH substitution, and parameterized instantiation via UnsupportedModuleConstructError; LOCAL via the same; and an EXTENDS naming a non-standard module with no findable .tla via UnresolvedExtendsError. analyze() propagates these; run() and gate_report() catch them and fail closed (nonzero / gate FAIL with the reason). This honours references/architecture_tractability.md "No Degenerate Escapes": when a model cannot be resolved, write the failure, not a smaller number. Measured alternatives and the self-scrutiny check: the risk flagged for this ticket was a resolver that appears to work on a model where the extended declarations do not matter to the bound. The regression fixture is deliberately the opposite -- Channel EXTENDS Counter, where the EXTENDED module carries the only bound-bearing variable (tick in 0..3) and the extending module adds only an unconstrained channel variable. Pre-fix the analyzer reports variables= ['emitted'], bound=1, Bump absent; post-fix variables={tick,emitted}, bound=4, Bump present. The number moves 1->4 and the assertions were run against the HEAD analyzer to confirm they fail pre-fix. Shipped example re-measured (examples/distributed_history, External EXTENDS Internal EXTENDS Core, no TypeInvariant so bound is 1 both ways): its verdict stays FAIL but the diagnosis is corrected from a spurious "C2 {responses} touched by 9 actions" (an artifact of seeing only External's 4 variables) to the true "C1 {accounts,carts,orders, responses} touched by 13 actions" over all 10 variables, with named port-crossing actions and modularity 0.000 -> 0.230. That corrected figure is relevant to MF-037 and the ticket-workflow example: any downstream copy of the old 9-action number is stale. entries.narrative: MF-036 makes the complexity check ADVISORY. A probe built a plain 5-variable, 10-command god-object CLI (recorded under results/probe/GodObjectCli.tla) and ran `analyze complexity`; it HARD-FAILED with "component C1 is touched by 10 actions, exceeding max_component_actions 8" (exit 1). Any program with more than eight commands over shared state failed the same way -- i.e. most real programs. Per owner direction 2026-07-20 and references/architecture_tractability.md ("Advisory, Not Blocking"), complexity is a scanner, not a gate. What changed (scripts only, zero TLA delta): (1) Every complexity threshold breach -- state-space bound, component variables, component actions, and the TLC distinct-states check -- is now an advisory WARNING that names the component/variable/action and RECOMMENDS a concrete move (e.g. "split the densest state <v> into its own component"). `analyze complexity` exits 0 whenever it can analyze the model; it exits nonzero ONLY when it CANNOT analyze it (the MF-030 fail-closed on an unresolved EXTENDS/INSTANCE hierarchy). "I could not measure this" stays an error; "this is complex" is now a finding. (2) Case generation no longer refuses above threshold. `enforce_complexity_gate` became `advise_complexity`: it prints the warnings and proceeds. The `--allow-over-budget` override was removed entirely -- there is no gate left to override. (3) Frame-condition accuracy fix: `v' = v` (the written-out form of UNCHANGED) was counted as a read AND a write, so every variable an action leaves alone showed as coupled to it. It is now stripped. On the GodObjectCli probe this drops the over-reported god-state from all five variables at 10/10 to the real coupling (only the shared `status` at 10/10; the four domain vars at 3/3/2/2), and the R/W interaction graph de-densifies from the complete graph (10 edges) to a star (4 edges). refinement.detail: Three reductions were considered against the landed design and all three were rejected on fidelity grounds -- each would have made a report LOOK cleaner while measuring less. (1) Treat an intra-component code edge as a convergence, collapsing the report to two categories instead of four. Rejected: with a one-component map every edge is then a convergence and the tool reports a perfect score for a codebase it never constrained. Internal edges are counted and explicitly NOT checked against a port. (2) Downgrade the extraction blind spots (dynamic imports, unparsed files, non-Python files, unmapped modules) from `unmappable` to a warning attached to a `coherent` verdict -- the smaller state space and the friendlier report. Rejected; this is MF-027 verbatim: a clean report on a target you could not see is indistinguishable from a clean report on one you could. The dogfood shows the cost of the decision honestly -- this repository's own scripts/ tree has zero divergences under a falsifiable partition and STILL reports unmappable, for three computed-name imports, one shell script, and one sibling package. (3) Drop the `unfalsifiable_coherence` check, on the argument that a fully ported architecture with no divergences is simply coherent. Rejected after measuring it: under the three-component partition this ticket first wrote, this repository's model ports every pair, so no code edge could have diverged and `coherent` would have been true by construction. That is the same false clean as (2), arriving through the model instead of the extractor. entries.narrative: AC-02 implements the reflexion model (Murphy, Notkin & Sullivan) on top of AC-01's descriptor: a DECLARED map from production modules to model components, an extracted Python dependency graph, and a diff reported as convergences, divergences (with file:line at the SITE of the dependency), and absences. Internal edges are counted as a fourth category and deliberately not checked -- they crossed no boundary. Shipped as scripts/architecture_reflexion.py, wired into `analyze architecture --code <tree> --map <map.yaml>`, with its own JSON schema (tla-spec-dev/architecture-reflexion v1) and a standalone CLI. Half a check is a usage error: --code without --map would make the TOOL pick the boundary, and --map without --code reports every port absent. THE DELIVERABLE IS THE DOGFOOD, and it took three runs to state honestly. Full write-up in results/dogfood-findings.txt; the short form: 1. The acceptance command as the plan wrote it -- no declared partition -- reports `unmappable` and does not run the diff at all. The model has one component (Q = 0.000; lastCommand and result are written by all fifteen commands). Had the diff run, all 258 code edges would have been internal to that single component: 0 divergences, 0 absences, `coherent`. The report prints "NOT RUN" instead of three zeroes, because zero findings from a comparison that never happened is the false clean in its purest form. This is the branch AC-01 published partition.consumable_as_architecture for, used exactly as intended. 2. With a DECLARED four-component partition (surface / tickets / corpus / kill, cut by the state each command commits) the check runs and is FALSIFIABLE: corpus<->kill and kill<->tickets have no port, because no action of the model touches kill_test together with ticket_state or with a corpus verdict. 34 modules all mapped, 4 components all realized, 258 edges, 140 internal, 118 convergences, 0 divergences, 0 absences. The two kill-test scripts reach only budgets.py, which is in surface and ported. That is a genuine falsifiable negative result about this codebase. The verdict is still `unmappable`, now for five extraction blind spots: three computed-name importlib.import_module calls, scripts/run_tlc.sh (no extractor), and spec_double_compiler/ (first-party, beside the code root, outside --code). 3. The COARSER three-component partition this ticket wrote first -- folding kill_test in with the other scanner verdicts, an entirely natural reading -- ports every pair, so no code edge could diverge and `coherent` would have been true by construction. `unfalsifiable_coherence` fires and refuses it. Runs 2 and 3 are both defensible readings of the same model, separated by one variable's placement. That is the ticket's central caution and it is stated in the reference rather than buried: the map and the partition are where the lying would happen, the tool measures the declaration it is handed, and it cannot audit that declaration. What it CAN do it does -- the map must place every module in the tree (leaving one out is `unmapped_module`, never cleaner), every declared component must be realized, no module may be in two components, and every placement is published. `unfalsifiable_coherence` catches only the fully degenerate case; a merely COARSE partition still reports a real-looking clean, and that limitation is documented. MF-027 is enforced structurally, not by convention. The verdict property reads nothing but the report: no environment variable, no flag, no manifest key. Suppression-shaped keys in the map (assume_coherent, allow_unmapped, waived, justification, accepted_divergences, ignore, exclude, skip, trusted, override, ...) are SCANNED, reported under ignored_suppression_keys, and never honored -- the shape scripts/effect_conformance.py uses, because a silently ignored key is nearly as bad as an honored one. TestNothingDowngradesAnUnobservableVerdict holds it shut from four directions: sixteen map keys, four environment variables, four plausible CLI flags (argparse rejects them), and a source-level assertion that the verdict property mentions no configuration at all. Evidence: results/suppression-ignored.txt, the same tree run twice with identical findings. A positive case exists, which matters because without one "always unmappable" would have passed every refusal test in the suite. The fixture is a three-component pipeline model whose ports permit ingest<->transform and transform<->deliver but not ingest<->deliver, with matching code: results/fixture-coherent.txt reports `coherent` with the unported pair named, so the clean result is falsifiable. results/fixture-divergent.txt adds one import and reports both the import and the call site with file:line; results/fixture-absence.txt removes an edge and reports the dead port. Advisory throughout. Exit 0 on `divergent` AND on `unmappable`; nonzero (2) only for an unusable map or an unreadable code tree -- "I could not measure this". No close, promotion, or case-generation path reads architecture_scan. CD-01 holds: the report names edges, ports, and files, and never says where a module should live; a test asserts the rendered text carries no move-suggesting phrasing. Coverage limits are stated in the report itself rather than left to be discovered: Python only; static resolution only; in-tree edges only, so a component that reaches a database or a socket directly is invisible (that axis belongs to scripts/effect_conformance.py). One limit was FOUND by the dogfood and fixed: imports resolving to a first-party package beside the code root were being filed as third-party, which meant narrowing --code would delete real edges from the graph with nothing recorded. They are now a named blind spot.

entries.narrative: AC-03 is the generation-time half of the epic: a descriptor is advice until it constrains the request. It ships prompts/implementation_brief.md (with templates/implementation_brief.md as the rendered shape) and prompts/aspect_decomposition.md, in the form prompts/coverage_audit.md established, plus the case-module/feature-module distinction stated once in SKILL.md under the Program Spec Rule. ZERO model delta, as the plan expected: ticket current == desired byte for byte, TLC green reproducing AC-01's figures exactly, and all three of specs/current, ticket current and ticket desired measuring 10 variables / 16 actions / 1 component / Q = 0.000. See results/model-delta.txt. THE DEMONSTRATION. Four briefs were rendered end-to-end by following the prompt, and they are kept as evidence because the interesting result is the spread, not any one of them: * OpenTicket, specs/current under a DECLARED 2-component partition (workflow | scanners) -- DEGRADED. Real constraints: writes only ticket_state/lastCommand/result, internal to workflow so it may not touch the scanner component at all, one declared effect port (spec_tree: filesystem.write **/specs/**), does not span so one commit point, and three of the variables it writes flagged as not single-writer. * AnalyzeComplexity, same descriptor, subject component named by the caller -- DEGRADED on two counts. Same partition, but the subject component owns nothing and has no internal action, so "this work belongs to scanners" restricts nothing by itself. The strongest clause in that brief is the measured SPAN: the action commits lastCommand/result in workflow and complexity_gate in scanners in one step, and the brief says the model asserts those land atomically -- honor it or report the model wrong. * OpenTicket, specs/current under the EMERGENT partition -- REFUSED, and the refusal artifact records verbatim what the vacuous brief would have said ("component C1, 10 of 10 variables, reaches nothing, zero violations"), so the failure mode is legible rather than theoretical. * CreateAccount, examples/distributed_history/.../Internal.tla, EMERGENT -- the only FULL brief, and it clears crossing_action_fraction by exactly zero. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE EPIC'S WORKING ASSUMPTIONS, both measured here. (1) AC-01's `consumable_as_architecture` is necessary but NOT sufficient for a non-vacuous brief. It is `partition_source == "declared" or decomposes`, which is right for AC-02 -- whose question is whether the project named a boundary to compare code against -- and wrong as AC-03's only gate, because it is true for ANY declared partition including a deliberately useless one. The prompt therefore layers three per-render vacuity tests on top of it: V1 (one component) refuses; V2 (the subject component owns nothing AND has no internal action) and V3 (crossing fraction > 0.5) degrade rather than refuse, because the write-set, effect-port and atomicity clauses are measured PER ACTION and survive a bad partition intact. The two DEGRADED renders above differ by exactly V2, from the same descriptor -- whether a brief constrains anything depends on which component the work lands in, not only on the partition score. (2) "Neither real model decomposes" is not what was measured. Internal.tla decomposes EMERGENTLY (2 components, Q = 0.0069, crossing fraction 0.50), and exhaustive search finds decomposing partitions of specs/current itself. See `refinement:` above and AC-03-DF-02. The refusal doctrine survives intact -- refusing to invent a cut is still right -- but the wording claims more than a greedy search establishes. A THIRD, SMALLER FINDING, filed as AC-03-DF-01 and defended against in the prompt: for a one-component partition the JSON reports ownership.single_writer_violations as null WITH a stated reason, but components[0].owns as the bare empty list []. A consumer reads that as "owns nothing" -- a plausible architectural fact -- when it means "undefined here". The text renderer says NOT MEASURABLE; the machine-readable contract that AC-02 and AC-03 actually read does not. Gate A refuses before the field can be reached, which is why the guard is a gate and not a caveat. DOCTRINE. CD-01 holds: neither prompt proposes a cut, a refactor, a target shape or a next step. Move 3's shapes are the vocabulary the measured facts are STATED in -- the brief says "these are your declared ports", not "push effects to the edges"; "the model says these commit together", not "introduce a commit point". Both are advisory and gate nothing. The Program Spec Rule is not weakened: the aspect prompt forbids a case module from declaring any state, constant or action, requires EXTENDS over INSTANCE/LOCAL, and keeps the removal test (delete every case module and the program is still fully represented) as the rule rather than a note. WHAT IS NOT SHOWN, and both prompts say so in their own validation sections: nothing here measures whether a brief changes what a coding agent produces. The prompts make the ask derivable and checkable field by field. Whether a derivable ask yields more coherent code is an empirical question this ticket did not answer and could not -- it belongs to the epic's evaluation tickets. Until then a brief is a hypothesis with good provenance, not a result.
